correctness.rationale: For any member T of length 2h, reverse-complement forces ν₂(T)=initial 1-run r(T). Normalized mantissa m(T) lies in [1,3/2) when r=1 and [3/2,2) otherwise. For integral A/B, odd ratio forces equal r and 2/3 < m(A)/m(B) <3/2; even ratio forces r(A)>r(B), lexicographically m(A)>m(B), hence 1<ratio<2. This excludes precisely the proposed parity-separated shell intervals. For j>=1, E_j has 4^j+1 even members, O_j has (7·4^j−4)/12 odd members; X_k=(3/2)·4^k count is (19/36)·4^k+2k/3−7/9. The uniform piecewise linear partial-shell count has its smallest ratio at t=3/2, establishing the liminf for the infinite set, not by finite experiment. Independent enumeration of all 255 antipalindromes through length 16, 400 distinct integer quotients and eight exact shell boundaries agrees. The proof establishes only a one-sided bound for the full complement.

final_claim: For canonical even-length binary antipalindromes, the complement of integer quotients has lower natural density >=19/54; an explicit disjoint even/odd shell exclusion F has exact lower density 19/54 (no claim of sharp full-complement density).
limitations: Exact lower density 19/54 pertains only to exhibited forbidden F, not necessarily all unrepresentable integers.
